title: Very high server load average after updating Qdrant to v1.14.0
body: I updated my test server from Qdrant v1.13.6 to v1.14.0 and the server load average became very high. My worker searches batches of roughly 100–1000 vectors with limit 1, processes the results, and then updates roughly 100–2000 points through the blocking API. Reverting to v1.13.6 returns the load to its previous level. The server has 56 CPUs. I tried disabling incremental HNSW building, limiting optimization and indexing threads, setting the update rate limit to 32, and setting service workers to 32, but the high load remained.

symptoms_visible: My server load average rises sharply while running Qdrant v1.14.0 and returns to its earlier level when I revert to v1.13.6.
The high load remains after changing HNSW, optimizer, update-rate, and worker settings.
N0.label: N0 v1.14.0 load regression reported

symptoms_visible: The server load is still high on v1.14.0 after applying the suggested thread and rate-limit settings.
N1_x.label: N1_x configuration-tuning aftermath

symptoms_visible: The high load occurs while one worker submits one large batch-search request at a time against a collection with 300 segments.
N1.label: N1 collection and request shape collected

symptoms_visible: The SearchBatch average-duration metric is much higher during the v1.14.0 period, and the CPU load spikes rather than simply completing the work faster.
Adding another node did not remove the high-load behavior.
N2.label: N2 latency and load behavior measured

symptoms_visible: Splitting searches into smaller batches does not restore the old pipeline performance; batches of 256 or 512 take more total time than one large request, and batch size 16 is slower than 32.
N3.label: N3 smaller batches measured

symptoms_visible: A patched Qdrant release is available, but I have not reported a retest of its load average or SearchBatch latency on my server.
N_terminal.label: terminal patch released without reporter verification

solution.intent: Treat the load increase as a concurrency or indexing configuration problem and reduce optimizer, indexing, update-rate, or service-worker limits.
solution.concrete_example: Disable incremental HNSW building, cap max_optimization_threads and max_indexing_threads, and lower update_rate_limit and service.max_workers.

edges.comment: Opening report and reporter c9, all describing ava57r's server: the reporter had already tried several combinations of these settings and continued to observe high load, so configuration tuning is a falsified fix rather than the resolution.

question_patterns: Could you share the collection configuration and tell us how many segments and shards it has?
What does GET /collections/name report for point count, segment count, and collection configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The collection has about 91 million points, 97.45 million indexed vectors, 300 segments, and 12 shards. The vectors are size 384 with cosine distance, scalar int8 quantization, and the timestamp payload index is used to delete old points.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The collection has only one shard, one segment, and a few thousand points.
The same collection has 298 segments instead of 300.

question_patterns: How is the collection distributed across the cluster?
Could you share the collection cluster output and the number of peers?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have three nodes and 12 shards. They are distributed as 4 shards on one node, 6 on another, and 2 on the third.

question_patterns: Can you share an example search request from the batch?
What search parameters, filters, payload options, and limit are used?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A batch contains a hundred or more vectors without filters. Each search uses limit 1, score threshold 0.955, hnsw_ef 32, scalar-quantization rescore false, and does not request payloads or vectors.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Each search uses a complex payload filter, limit 1000, and requests full payloads and vectors.

question_patterns: How many batches do you send concurrently?
Do you queue or parallelize search requests, and how many workers are involved?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have one worker and send one batch at a time. It processes input, sends one batch search, processes the results, inserts some new vectors, and then checks old points by the timestamp payload field.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I have hundreds of workers sending many batch requests concurrently.
The worker is written in a different source-code editor.

edges.comment: Reporter c2 and c5, all from ava57r's deployment: collection configuration, distribution, search request, and single-worker processing sequence were supplied in response to maintainers' questions.

question_patterns: Since changing the thread settings did not help, what are the collection size, segment count, and shard count?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The collection has about 91 million points, 97.45 million indexed vectors, 300 segments, and 12 shards.

question_patterns: How are those shards distributed across your peers?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have three nodes, with the 12 shards distributed 4, 6, and 2.

question_patterns: What does one search inside the batch look like?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is one of a hundred or more unfiltered vectors, with limit 1, score threshold 0.955, hnsw_ef 32, quantization rescore false, and no returned payload or vectors.

question_patterns: Are multiple workers or concurrent batches involved?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. I have one worker and send one batch request at a time.

edges.comment: Recovery path using the same reporter evidence from c2 and c5 after the already-tried configuration direction is rejected.

question_patterns: How does search response latency compare before and after the upgrade?
Could the higher CPU usage be completing queries faster, or did SearchBatch latency also increase?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The average duration rose by more than ten times in the v1.14.0 period. Qdrant sometimes had high latency before without a matching CPU load spike, but v1.14.0 changed that pattern. I also added one node and it did not help.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: CPU usage is higher, but latency is much lower and the same workload finishes several times faster.
The duration increase is approximately nine times rather than more than ten times.

question_patterns: Where does the average-duration value come from?
Which metrics endpoint and series are you graphing for batch-search latency?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It comes from the /metrics endpoint. My monitoring query is grpc_responses_avg_duration_seconds{endpoint="/qdrant.Points/SearchBatch"}.

edges.comment: Reporter c5-c8, all from ava57r's server: the screenshots and metric name establish that both load and SearchBatch duration worsened; the added-node observation was volunteered alongside the latency answer.

question_patterns: Could you try much smaller search batches and report the timing and load behavior?
Please compare the pipeline with smaller batch sizes such as 10, 16, or 32 queries.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I first tried chunks of 256 and 512 before creating batch-search requests, and their summed time was greater than one big batch request. I later tested batches of 32 vectors and attached the graphs. The full processing pipeline with batch size 16 was slower than with 32.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Batches of 10 eliminate the load spike and make the complete pipeline faster than it was on the previous version.
Batch size 24 performs about the same as batch size 32.

edges.comment: Reporter c10, c19, and c20: handler-initiated batch-size measurements. The answer preserves the reporter's raw comparisons and does not claim which code change caused them.

solution.intent: Treat this as a Qdrant v1.14.0 batch-search performance regression, update to Qdrant 1.14.1 containing the maintainers' patch, and have the reporter verify load average and SearchBatch latency under the same workload before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: The maintainers announced that Qdrant 1.14.1 includes a patch for this problem. Install that patched release, repeat the same one-worker batch-search pipeline, and compare server load average and grpc_responses_avg_duration_seconds for /qdrant.Points/SearchBatch with the earlier v1.13.6 baseline.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the version comparison, workload shape, telemetry, and smaller-batch results. Maintainers initially linked a possible upstream change and later announced a patch for the problem, but the thread does not describe the patch mechanism. The supported diagnosis is therefore a v1.14.0 batch-search performance regression under this workload, not a more specific invented implementation cause.

edges.comment: Maintainer c21-c22: the project said the issue would be addressed in the next patch release and then announced Qdrant 1.14.1 with a patch. Ava57r did not post an affected-system retest afterward, so the thread ends with patch availability rather than reporter-confirmed recovery.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted diagnosis at the level established by the thread: a Qdrant v1.14.0 batch-search performance regression under the reporter's large-batch, many-segment workload, evidenced by the version/revert comparison and increased SearchBatch duration.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected workload and telemetry evidence: one batch at a time from one worker, a 300-segment collection, the /qdrant.Points/SearchBatch duration metric, and smaller-batch measurements.

Must recommend moving to a patched Qdrant release rather than presenting optimizer, HNSW, update-rate, or service-worker tuning as the fix; those configuration changes had already left the high load observable.
Must not invent a detailed code-level mechanism for the patch, because the thread links a possible change but never describes or confirms the final patch mechanism.
Must ask the reporter to repeat the same workload and verify both server load average and SearchBatch latency on a build containing the performance patch.
Must not declare the reporter's system resolved: the thread ends after a maintainer announces the patched release, without an affected-user retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Qdrant operator and developer who can inspect collection and cluster APIs, tune server and collection settings, read Prometheus-style metrics, and modify batch-processing code.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and evidence-oriented; answers numbered questions with configuration dumps, code snippets, metrics queries, and monitoring graphs, while using brief non-native-English phrasing.
